Python/PythonCodeAlong.html.title: Code-Along
Python/PythonCodeAlong.html.body:
Turtle Code-Along
In this introductory activity, use turtle graphics to create a drawing in Python!

Getting Started
Click here to go to HyTOP!

Give your project a name
Select "Python" as the Project Type
Click the "Create Project" button


Now you have a Python project!
Turtle Essentials
First, add the essential code for a basic turtle project.

In the code section on the left, add the following line to import everything from the turtle library: from turtle import *


Click the Run button in the top left, and notice that nothing happens yet
Make a new line under the import, and add the following code: shelly = Turtle()


shelly is now a Turtle object - but Shelly needs a shape! Under that line, add the following code to give Shelly a shape:   shelly.shape("arrow")


Run the code again to see Shelly appear on the screen!
BONUS: Update the code so that instead of an "arrow" shape, the turtle looks like a turtle

The code should look something like this:
from turtle import *

shelly = Turtle()
shelly.shape("arrow")

Adding Color
Make things a little more interesting by updating the colors.

Make a new line, and add code to change Shelly's color
HINT: this is a lot like how the shape was updated - just using color instead


On the next line, add the following code: paper = shelly.getscreen()


Now, the paper variable stores the screen. Change its color using bgcolor
BONUS: Play around with the settings to create a pleasing (or terrible) color scheme!

The added code should look something like this:
shelly.color("green")
paper = shelly.getscreen()
paper.bgcolor("gold")

Moving the Turtle
One of the most useful turtle abilities is the ability to move across the screen and draw like a pen! Create a blank line, and then add the following command on the next line:
shelly.forward(100)

Click the Run button to see the turtle move across the screen! Specifically, it moves forward 100 pixels in the direction it is currently facing (90 degrees).
It is also possible to turn the turtle. Add the following command on the next line:
shelly.right(90)

This command turns the turtle 90 degrees to the right. Previously the direction of the turtle was 90 degrees (pointing to the right), so after turning 90 degrees to the right, the turtle should face down (180 degrees).
Run the program again to see the turtle move to the right, then turn to face down!
Drawing a Square
Add the following commands to the file, under the existing commands:
shelly.forward(100)
shelly.right(90)
shelly.forward(100)
shelly.right(90)

Run the program to see what this code does. It should draw part of a square! How does that work? On a piece of paper, or on a whiteboard, try to draw the same square as the turtle:

Draw the top side from left to right
Turn the writing utensil and draw the right side from top to bottom
Turn the writing utensil and draw the bottom side from left to right

So, the turtle moves 100 pixels to the right, turns 90 degrees to face down, moves 100 pixels down, turns 90 degrees to face left, moves 100 pixels to the left, and then turns 90 degrees to face up!
The Rest of the Square
Complete the square that Shelly is drawing. The code will be the same as the first part of the square:
shelly.forward(100)
shelly.right(90)

Looping
At this point, there appears to be a lot of repeated lines of code. This isn't too big of a deal, but it could be annoying to change the size of the square, or draw a shape with more sides. Luckily, there is a way to automatically repeat commands: the for loop!
Looping the Square
Use a for loop to repeat the code that draws the square.

Identify the two lines of square-drawing code that repeat
shelly.forward and shelly.right


Notice how many times those two lines repeat: 4
Remove all repeated instances of that code, so there are only two commands remaining
Indent the two lines by adding a couple spaces in front of them
Above the two lines, not indented, add a for loop
It should start with for
Then, add x in
Then add range(4):
Note that it should repeat 4 times



The code should look something like this:
for x in range(4):
  shelly.forward(100)
  shelly.right(90)

Much shorter, and easier to maintain! Now, to change the size of the square, only one number has to be updated.
Drawing a Star
Another cool thing about for loops is they can repeat any number of times. Three or four times isn't that cool, but repeating 60 times can be very helpful! Use a for loop to draw another type of shape - a star.
Preparation
First, get to the proper location on the map (without drawing), and change the speed and color as well.

At the bottom of the file, make a new line
Add a command for Shelly to pick up the pen: shelly.penup()
Under that, add a command for Shelly to go to a new location: shelly.goto(-175, 75)
Under that, have Shelly put the pen back down: shelly.pendown()
Next, add a command to change Shelly's speed: shelly.speed(20)
Finally, change Shelly's color to make this shape special: shelly.color("purple")

The code for this part should look like this:
shelly.penup()
shelly.goto(-175, 75)
shelly.pendown()
shelly.speed(20)
shelly.color("purple")

For Loop
Now that Shelly is in position, create a new for loop that draws a star shape.

Make a new line at the bottom of the file
Create a for loop structure to repeat 60 times
Start with for
Then add x in
Finally, add range(60):


Under the for line, create a new indented line (add a couple spaces in front)
On the new indented line, move Shelly forward - 200 pixels
Under that, still indented, turn Shelly to the right - 186 pixels

The code should look something like this:
for x in range(60):
  shelly.forward(200)
  shelly.right(186)

Feel free to update the numbers to see how the star changes!
Hiding the Turtle
At the end, hide the turtle so that the star can be viewed with nothing in the way!
shelly.hideturtle()

Final Code
At the end of the code-along, the code should look something like this:
from turtle import *

shelly = Turtle()
shelly.shape("turtle")
shelly.color("green")

paper = shelly.getscreen()
paper.bgcolor("gold")

for x in range(4):
  shelly.forward(100)
  shelly.right(90)

shelly.penup()
shelly.goto(-175, 75)
shelly.pendown()
shelly.speed(20)
shelly.color("purple")

for x in range(60):
  shelly.forward(200)
  shelly.right(186)

shelly.hideturtle()

Congratulations! You've completed a Python Turtle program 🐢🐢🐢

ArtificialIntelligence/VibeDrawingWarmUp.title: Warm-Up: Vibe Drawing
ArtificialIntelligence/VibeDrawingWarmUp.body:
Warm-Up: Vibe Drawing
In this activity, use A.I. to generate code that makes a drawing!
Part One: Vibe Coding Python Turtle
First, get some code from ChatGPT.

Go to ChatGPT
Prompt it with "give me python turtle code that draws a picture of SOMETHING"
When it finishes spitting out the result, copy the code using the copy button in the upper right of the code block

Now you have some code!
Part Two: Running the Code
Next, create a new HyTOP Python project and paste the code.

Go to the HyTOP Create Project page
Enter a project name
Select "Python" as the project type
In the code editor under main.py, paste the code
Save the project with Ctrl+S or clicking the Save button in the upper left

Now you have a drawing!
Part Three: Iterating
The next step is to basically repeat the steps above. If your drawing isn't what you want, try asking ChatGPT to change it up. Then, copy the code again, remove all the existing code from the project, and paste the new code.
Side Note: Non-Vibe Coding
This process can get pretty frustrating if the A.I. does not understand what you mean, or makes changes you don't want. Sometimes, it's easier to actually look at the code, try to understand it, and change it yourself instead of relying on A.I.!
Part Four: SVG
Python Turtle graphics are one way to draw with code, but there are other ways too! One very powerful online graphics tool is Scalable Vector Graphics, or SVG.
Repeat the process above, but with SVG instead of Python! This will require a few key changes:

The prompt needs to ask for an html document that includes an svg element that shows a picture of SOMETHING
The HyTOP project has to be a Web (HTML) project instead of a Python Project

Try out some different ideas to see what ChatGPT + SVG can do!
Part Five: Submission
When you have a drawing you like, either through Python + Turtle or HTML + SVG, submit your project! Form linked from the course homepage.

ArtificialIntelligence/VibeArchitecture..title: Vibe Architecture
ArtificialIntelligence/VibeArchitecture..body:
Vibe Architecture
In this activity, try to think about what software you might be able to build if you could build anything. You are not limited by your skills, only your imagination!
Part One: Blue Sky Brainstorming (15m)
Think about what you might want to make. The only criteria is that it has to be software. Utilize the blue sky thinking technique - basically, there are no bad ideas. You may find later that there certainly are bad ideas, but to start, pretend there could never be a bad idea.
Here are some software ideas:

A game
A social media app
A personal website
An immersive art piece

Part Two: Engineering (15m)
The next part is where skills are required. It may be tempting to just say "hey ChatGPT build my idea" but that's not always going to work!

Luckily, A.I. is pretty good at figuring out how to do something if it knows what it's doing very specifically.

Go to ChatGPT
Give it your ideas
Ask it about feasibility
Ask it about frameworks
Ask it about architecture
Ask it about tools
Ask it to teach you about these things
Ask it how you can get started

Note that none of this is Vibe Coding, because it does not involve code at all - it's more like creating plans / blueprints.
Part Three: Implementation (15m)
Now for the part where you try to actually bring something into existence. This is where it gets especially tricky, because you may have to download / install software or actually get something up and running. You might be able to host your project in HyTOP, but most software applications require a bit more than just front-end HTML/CSS/JS or front-end Python.
That said, ask ChatGPT to give you some code, and see what happens! If things aren't working, go back and ask how to fix them.
Side-note: Context
Context is extremely important when speaking with chatbots. In fact, since LLMs are basically just giant auto-completes, the context you provide does a lot to determine output. Some important items to provide:

Your experience level with different technologies
Your goals in building your piece of software / learning
The capabilities of HyTOP and your current computer
The software you have downloaded / installed

Conclusion
Hopefully, by the end of this activity, you will have some idea of the power AND the limitations of an A.I. software development workflow. You might even have something cool to show, even if it's just a prototype or one piece of something larger!

ArtificialIntelligence/FurtherReading.ht.title: Further Reading
ArtificialIntelligence/FurtherReading.ht.body:
Further Reading
Go deep on any of these topics with the resources provided below. Wikipedia
History
The history of A.I. goes back to antiquity. This list of articles touches on a few selected highlights.

Wikipedia: History of A.I.
IBM: History of A.I.

The Turing Test
A landmark paper in the early study of artificial intelligence. Designed by Alan Turing, it was meant to test if a machine had achieved actual intelligence.

Read about the test
Take the test live

ELIZA
One of the earliest and most significant examples of a chatbot, ELIZA was developed from 1964 to 1967 at MIT by Joseph Weizenbaum.

The ELIZA effect: a tendency to project human traits — such as experience, semantic comprehension or empathy — onto rudimentary computer programs having a textual interface
Chat with ELIZA

A.I. Defeats a Chess Grandmaster
In 1997, Deep Blue became the first computer to defeat a world champion in Chess.
Technology
The technologies involved in artificial intelligence are interesting and varied. Generally, when people say "A.I." in 2025, they are referring to generative A.I.. Almost always, these tools are built on large language models or involve some form of deep learning.

Essential Terminology
A.I. Learns to play Super Mario World
This is made possible by Reinforcement Learning: one subset of ML


A.I. Agents

Computer Brains
A.I. systems often closely resemble humans in their ability to communicate. Neural networks serve as the basis for deep learning, which powers most A.I. tools today.

Cognitive Revolution: psychology inspired by computers, inspiring computers inspired by psychology
Complete map of a Fruit Fly brain

Philosophy
There are several fascinating areas of thought surrounding artificial intelligence.
Can a machine understand anything?
Chinese room thought experiment
Can a machine actually experience anything?
Hard problem of consciousness
What constitutes "true" A.I.?
A.I. effect
Can a machine achieve human-level intelligence?
Artificial general intelligence
What are the long-term risks of A.I.?
Existential risk
How can we keep A.I. safe?
A.I. safety
How do we know A.I. will act in our best interest?
A.I. alignment
What might happen if an A.I. system is misaligned?
Paperclip maximizer
How fast could A.I. improve itself?
Recursive self-improvement
How smart could A.I. actually become?
Superintelligence
Will we experience a technological singularity within our lifetime?
Technological singularity

EmergingTechnology/SpeculativeFiction.ht.title: Speculative Fiction
EmergingTechnology/SpeculativeFiction.ht.body:
Speculative Fiction
Imagine a future in which some emerging or hypothetical technology has advanced beyond its current state. What will this technology be able to do? How might one individual be impacted by these new things? What is within the realm of possibility?
Your Goal
Write a short story, journal entry, screen play, or anything else set in a near- or far-future world. When you're done, click here to share your story.
Story Bones
Before starting, you will want to make some key decisions:

What year is it?
Where does the story take place?
Who is the main character?
Which technology is impacting the world?

If you want help, click here for a random prompt generator.
